channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: National Library Parking Project Lacks Environmental Impact Assessment, Says Committee
item.description: Uzbekistan's National Committee for Ecology and Climate Change stated that no environmental impact assessment exists for the planned parking lot project behind the National Library. The committee emphasized that construction impacting green spaces requires prior ecological evaluation, warning against replacing mature trees.

item.title: Taliban Report Over 300 Families Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced that 354 families, totaling 1,560 individuals, were forcibly returned to Afghanistan on the previous day. Returns occurred through multiple border crossings, including Torkham in Nangarhar, Spin Boldak in Kandahar, Silk Bridge in Nimroz, and Islam Qala in Herat.

item.title: ECO Industry Ministers Meet in Dushanbe for Fourth Session
item.description: The fourth ministerial meeting on industry for Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) member states convened in Dushanbe on September 23, 2026. The meeting, held within the Second International Textile Forum 'Tajikistan 2026', aimed to boost economic integration and industrial partnerships. Representatives from nine countries and international organizations attended.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Monitors Issyk-Kul Water Quality at Various Depths
item.description: Specialists from Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations are conducting hydrochemical monitoring of Issyk-Kul's water quality at different depths. The monitoring will take place from September 21 to 27, 2026, assessing the lake's water composition.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Deputy Proposes Public Chamber for Election Monitoring
item.description: Deputy Gulya Kozhokulova proposed establishing a public chamber for observers to monitor elections in real-time. This initiative aims to allow citizens to oversee voting processes at polling stations through live feeds.

item.title: Kyiv hit by missile strike, causing casualties and damage to infrastructure
item.description: A missile strike on Kyiv on September 24, 2026, resulted in two deaths and six injuries, according to Deutsche Welle citing the city's mayor. Fragments damaged residential buildings, a maternity ward's parking area, and a diagnostic center. Telegram channel Insider UA reported approximately 20 missiles were launched, targeting energy infrastructure.

item.title: Asian Development Bank forecasts strong economic growth for Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The Asian Development Bank's September outlook projects Kyrgyzstan's economy to grow by 8.9 percent in 2026 and 8.4 percent in 2027. This forecast indicates a positive economic trajectory for the country in the coming years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's meat imports significantly exceed exports
item.description: In January-July 2026, Kyrgyzstan's trade in meat and edible offal showed a significant imbalance, with import purchases exceeding $56 million. This figure is 32.67 times greater than the republic's exports, according to the National Statistical Committee.

item.title: New Regulations for Vehicle Evacuation and Impound Lots in Tashkent
item.description: Tashkent is introducing new procedures for the evacuation, placement, and storage of vehicles seized for legal violations. A unified electronic system will manage seized cars, allowing for online payment of fines and fees. This pilot project, running until December 2034, aims to streamline the process and integrate with tax authorities.

item.title: Afghanistan Defeats Host Japan by 48 Runs in Asian Games Cricket Opener
item.description: Afghanistan began its Asian Games men's cricket campaign with a 48-run victory over host Japan. Afghanistan scored 129 for six, and their bowlers restricted Japan to 81. Arab Gul took four wickets for eight runs, securing a winning start for Afghanistan in Group A.

item.title: Russia Claims Interception of Over 35 Ukrainian Drones
item.description: Russia's Ministry of Defense reported intercepting and shooting down at least 35 Ukrainian drones launched during the day. State media TASS stated that Russian air defense systems neutralized the drones over Belgorod, Bryansk, Kursk regions, Bashkortostan, and Crimea.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Path is Clarity, Good Neighborliness, and Dialogue, Says Saida Mirziyoyeva
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, stated at the UN General Assembly that Uzbekistan's firm position is clarity, good neighborliness, and dialogue in a world of increasing conflict and decreasing trust. She emphasized peace, cooperation, and human dignity.

item.title: Pakistan conducts airstrikes in Afghanistan following alleged drone incursions
item.description: Pakistan reported carrying out airstrikes on 10 locations in Afghanistan early Thursday. The strikes were a retaliation for alleged drone attacks launched from Afghan territory into Pakistan the previous day, according to Pakistan's information minister. The Taliban stated the attacks caused no damage.

item.title: Iranian and Pakistani Foreign Ministers Meet in New York
item.description: The foreign ministers of Iran and Pakistan held a meeting in New York. The details of their discussions were not immediately available, but the meeting likely addressed regional issues and bilateral relations between the two countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan establishes diplomatic relations with Vanuatu
item.description: Uzbekistan and Vanuatu have signed a joint communique to establish diplomatic relations in New York. The document was signed by Uzbekistan's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ulugbek Lapasov, and Vanuatu's Head of Mission to the UN, Odo Tevi. Both sides emphasized strengthening cooperation within international organizations.

item.title: Pakistan strikes 10 Afghan sites after accusing Taliban of drone incursion
item.description: Pakistan conducted precision aerial and drone strikes against 10 locations in Afghanistan, stating it was in self-defense after accusing the Taliban of launching drones into Pakistani territory. Pakistan's information minister described the strikes as "deliberate, precise, calibrated and proportionate," targeting military sites linked to the alleged drone attacks.

item.title: CSTO Foreign Ministers Held Working Meeting in New York
item.description: Foreign ministers from Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) member states convened a working meeting in New York on September 23, 2026. The meeting, chaired by the Russian Federation, discussed preparations for the upcoming Council of Collective Security meeting and priorities of Russia's CSTO chairmanship. An initiative by Belarus and Russia on a Eurasian Charter for Diversity and Multipolarity was also addressed.

item.title: Pakistan Conducts Air and Drone Strikes in Afghanistan After Taliban Attacks
item.description: Pakistan's information minister announced air and drone strikes on 10 Afghan locations in retaliation for alleged Taliban drone attacks. The strikes were described as a sovereign right to self-defense, deliberate, precise, calculated, and proportionate, targeting only military sites linked to attacks on Pakistan. Islamabad warned the Taliban against further attacks from Afghan territory.

item.title: OpenAI to Provide Free Cyber Defense Tools to Ukraine
item.description: OpenAI will offer its AI-powered Daybreak cyber defense system free of charge to Ukraine. The company aims to help protect Ukraine's civilian infrastructure, including hospitals and power plants, from cyberattacks. The announcement was made via a link to further details on daryo.uz.

item.title: Pakistan Attacks 10 Afghan Locations; Taliban Claims No Casualties
item.description: Pakistan launched attacks on 10 points across Afghanistan. The Taliban reported that the strikes did not result in any casualties. The nature and specific locations of the attacks were not detailed.

item.title: New technologies double cotton yield at Agrocluster Oltingul
item.description: Uzbekistan's Agrocluster Oltingul has doubled cotton yields using Xinjiang technology on 23 hectares of its 850-hectare fields. This method, involving double-row planting under film and drip irrigation, saves water by 40% and fertilizer by 30%. The initiative aligns with a December 2025 presidential decree aimed at boosting crop yields and resource efficiency in agriculture.

item.title: UNDP Constructs 205 Earthquake-Resistant Buildings in Nangarhar with South Korean Aid
item.description: The UNDP has built 205 earthquake-resistant buildings in Nangarhar, Afghanistan, with support from South Korea. The structures include homes and health centers, with 203 housing vulnerable families. The project also created jobs for 719 locals and restored irrigation for 500 acres of farmland.

item.title: Artificial intelligence center for youth established in Balykchy
item.description: An artificial intelligence center for youth has been established in Balykchy, Kyrgyzstan, following a presidential decree. The center, created by "Akademiya IT Star," aims to develop digitalization services export and provide IT training in marketing, programming, and robotics. It has created 100 jobs and offers IT services to over 500 businesses.

item.title: Intensive technologies boost fish farming efficiency in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A fish farming project utilizing intensive technologies has been launched by "Chinobod real biznes" in Balykchy district, Kyrgyzstan. The project, costing 30 billion soms, produces 200 tons of fish meat and 2.5 million fry annually on a two-hectare area. It also includes a laboratory for water purification using chlorella.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva attends UN session, holds meetings in New York
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of the Presidential Administration of Uzbekistan, attended the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York. She held bilateral meetings with the CEO of the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) to discuss joint projects in transport and healthcare, and with Google's Vice President regarding YouTube monetization.

item.title: Central Asian Experts Discuss Future of Regional Cooperation Amid Global Changes
item.description: An international expert meeting on Central Asia's independent strategies, regional security, and new cooperation formats was held in Cadenabbia, Italy. Organized by the Konrad Adenauer Foundation, the event gathered experts from the region to discuss what shapes Central Asian identity and the future of regional partnerships.

item.title: Balykchy Enterprise Produces Sports Equipment Meeting International Standards
item.description: The 'LB Sport' enterprise in Balykchy, Kyrgyzstan, manufactures sports equipment according to international standards, replacing imports. The project, costing 25 billion soums, produces 65 types of equipment for 18 sports, with an annual output of 500,000 units worth 75 billion soums. Exports reach $3 million annually to Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and CIS countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan actively prepares for the 5th Samarkand Human Rights Forum
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively preparing for the 5th Samarkand Human Rights Forum, scheduled for September 28-29 in Tashkent and Samarkand. The forum will focus on human rights, sustainable development, and international cooperation, marking anniversaries of key human rights pacts and declarations.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Meets Residents and Entrepreneurs on Andijan Gastronomy Street
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev engaged with residents and entrepreneurs on Andijan's gastronomy street in the Orikzor neighborhood. The 1.2-kilometer street created 100 new jobs and can accommodate over 10,000 visitors daily.

item.title: Two Afghan Citizens Enter US Via Legal Exception to Refugee Policy
item.description: Afghan Evacuate (AfghanIOM) reports two Afghan citizens entered the US through a legal exception to current policies, utilizing the refugee admission program. AfghanIOM's director stated this admission served US national interests. Thousands of Afghans await resettlement.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev visits ecotourism complex in Asaka
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited an ecotourism complex in Asaka. Once fully operational, the facility is expected to provide 80 billion soums in services annually and contribute 3 billion soums to the local budget.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Dies of Poisoning in Istanbul After Unofficial Treatment
item.description: An Uzbek citizen, Mohirano Meliyeva, died in Istanbul on September 19 due to poisoning from pharmaceutical agents. She was being treated at home by unofficial doctors, which worsened her condition. Despite being taken to hospital, doctors could not save her life. Her body was repatriated.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Reviews Xinjiang Cotton Growing Method Using Drip Irrigation
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev reviewed the Xinjiang method of cotton cultivation, which uses drip irrigation and fertilization systems to deliver water and nutrients directly to the plant roots. This method reportedly saves up to 40% of water and nearly 30% of fertilizer.

item.title: Bishkek Residents Learn About Eco-Friendly Heating Systems
item.description: An informational meeting was held in Bishkek for residents interested in eco-friendly and energy-efficient heating systems, specifically heat pumps. Participants learned about preferential state loans for installation, equipment costs, and operational benefits, including during electricity supply restrictions. The project is supported by the World Bank.

item.title: Bishkek residents learn about eco-friendly heating systems
item.description: An informational meeting in Bishkek focused on state subsidized loans for eco-friendly heating systems. Attendees learned about loan conditions, borrower requirements, and eligible expenses. A supplier presented heat pump technology, its benefits, and installation. The project is supported by the World Bank.

item.title: US, Denmark, and Greenland sign defense agreement to expand US military presence
item.description: The US, Denmark, and Greenland have signed a security agreement allowing the US to expand its military presence on the island. The deal amends a 1951 defense treaty and could lead to two additional US military bases.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Kochkor District Still Addressing Aftermath of July Mudflows
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Emergency Situations visited Kochkor district in Naryn region to assess the consequences of July mudflows. Four out of five affected state railway sections are cleared, with plans for protective measures on the remaining one and a new mudflow channel.

item.title: Iranian President: We are not afraid of war, nor do we shy away from negotiation
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated at the UN General Assembly that Iran is not afraid of war for self-defense and does not avoid negotiation for peace. He asserted that threats strengthen the Iranian nation and that they will not accept the language of force.

item.title: Journalist's Trial in Bishkek Postponed Due to Absent Experts
item.description: A Bishkek court postponed the retrial of journalist Makhabat Tajibek kyzy because key experts failed to appear. Defense questioned an expert's competence, while the prosecution cited language day events and illness. The case relates to media projects Temirov LIVE and Ait, Ait.

item.title: Journalist's Trial Postponed Due to Expert Absence in Bishkek
item.description: A Bishkek court postponed the retrial of journalist Makhabat Tajibek Kyzy because key experts failed to appear. One expert was attending a state language event, another was on sick leave. The defense questioned an expert's competence. The Supreme Court previously ordered a review of her case.
